import { Link as AriaLink } from 'react-aria-components'
import type { LinkProps as AriaLinkProps } from 'react-aria-components'

import {
  LINK,
  LINK_CAPS,
  LINK_CAPS_BASE,
  LINK_URL,
  LINK_VIEWMORE,
} from '../link'

/** Which of the sheet's three links this is. */
export type LinkVariant = 'caps' | 'url' | 'viewmore'

/** `.ds-link-caps--lg` only changes the type size, so it is a size rather than a second variant. */
export type LinkSize = 'sm' | 'lg'

export interface LinkProps extends Omit<
  AriaLinkProps,
  'className' | 'href' | 'isDisabled' | 'onPress' | 'target'
> {
  /** Where the link goes. It renders a real anchor, so middle-click and "open in a new tab" work. */
  href?: AriaLinkProps['href']
  /** Renders it unavailable without removing it from the page. */
  isDisabled?: AriaLinkProps['isDisabled']
  /** Press handler. This is a React Aria prop — there is no `onClick`. */
  onPress?: AriaLinkProps['onPress']
  /** The anchor's target, e.g. `_blank`. */
  target?: AriaLinkProps['target']

  /**
   * `caps` is `.ds-link-caps` — the sheet's nav and legend link. `url` is `.ds-link-url`, for a
   * destination inside running text. `viewmore` is `.ds-link-viewmore`, the accent call to go and
   * read the rest.
   */
  variant?: LinkVariant
  /** Only `caps` has two sizes, because only `.ds-link-caps` does. */
  size?: LinkSize
  className?: string
  children?: React.ReactNode
}

/**
 * The sheet's three links: `.ds-link-caps`, `.ds-link-url` and `.ds-link-viewmore`.
 *
 * ```tsx
 * <Link href="/monitors" isCurrent>Monitors</Link>
 * <Link variant="url" href="https://status.example.com">status.example.com</Link>
 * <Link variant="viewmore" href="/monitors">View more</Link>
 * ```
 *
 * React Aria's `Link` is what makes these links at all: it renders a real `<a>`, so middle-click,
 * the status bar and "open in a new tab" work, and `isCurrent` gives the page you are on both
 * `aria-current` for a screen reader and `data-current` for the sheet's own
 * `[aria-current="page"] { color: teal }` rule.
 *
 * **The three variants are three different jobs, which is why they are not one link with a colour
 * option.** Every one of them derives its hover from what it is: a caps link darkens toward full
 * strength because at 70% it is deliberately quiet at rest; a URL link turns teal because its
 * underline already carries the affordance; and a view-more link *gains* an underline, because it
 * wears the accent at rest and needs somewhere to go on hover. Swapping any two of those would say
 * the wrong thing about the link.
 */
export function Link({
  variant = 'caps',
  size = 'sm',
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: LinkProps) {
  const variantClass =
    variant === 'url'
      ? LINK_URL
      : variant === 'viewmore'
        ? LINK_VIEWMORE
        : [LINK_CAPS[size], LINK_CAPS_BASE].join(' ')

  return (
    <AriaLink
      data-slot="link"
      className={[LINK, variantClass, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </AriaLink>
  )
}

/**
 * The sheet's links. Three treatments, each with its own hover — the sheet varies the *treatment*
 * rather than the colour, which is why these are variants and not one link with a size on it.
 *
 * All three are written against a real `<a>`: React Aria's `Link` renders one, so the middle-click,
 * the status bar, "open in a new tab" and the browser's own visited styling all work. A `div` with
 * an `onClick` is the thing this avoids.
 */
export const LINK = [
  'cursor-pointer bg-transparent',
  'transition-[color,background-color,text-decoration-color] duration-[120ms]',
  'ease-pulse',
  'data-[focus-visible]:outline-1 data-[focus-visible]:outline-offset-2',
  'data-[focus-visible]:outline-teal',
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-link-caps`: 14px, `-0.01em`, uppercase, white at 70% going to white on hover.
 * `lg` is its `.ds-link-caps--lg`, which changes the type size and nothing else.
 */
export const LINK_CAPS: Record<'sm' | 'lg', string> = {
  sm: 'text-[14px]',
  lg: 'text-[16px]',
}

/** The rest of `.ds-link-caps`, shared by both sizes. */
export const LINK_CAPS_BASE = [
  'tracking-[-0.01em] uppercase',
  'text-fg/70',
  'hover:text-fg data-[hovered]:text-fg',
  // The page you are on, from the sheet's own `[aria-current="page"] { color: teal }`.
  'data-[current]:text-teal',
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-link-url`: 12px, `-0.015em`, underlined, going teal on hover. The underline is
 * the whole affordance — it is the one link here that sits inside running text, where a colour
 * change alone would not mark it.
 */
export const LINK_URL = [
  'text-[12px] tracking-[-0.015em] text-fg',
  'underline decoration-1 underline-offset-[3px]',
  'hover:text-teal hover:decoration-teal',
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-link-viewmore`: 16px, uppercase, in the accent — and the one link that *gains*
 * its underline on hover rather than losing it. It is a call to go and look at the rest, so it
 * wears the accent at rest and underlines itself when the pointer arrives.
 */
export const LINK_VIEWMORE = [
  'text-[16px] tracking-[-0.01em] uppercase text-teal',
  'no-underline',
  'hover:underline hover:underline-offset-4',
].join(' ')

docs:
A trail back up the hierarchy, where the last step is the page you are on.

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs label="Breadcrumb">
  <Breadcrumbs.Item href="/monitors">Monitors</Breadcrumbs.Item>
  <Breadcrumbs.Item href="/monitors/fra1">fra1</Breadcrumbs.Item>
  <Breadcrumbs.Item>Frankfurt</Breadcrumbs.Item>
</Breadcrumbs>
```

| Slot               | React Aria    | Notes                                                       |
| ------------------ | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumbs`      | `Breadcrumbs` | The trail. `label` names the `<nav>`                        |
| `Breadcrumbs.Item` | `Breadcrumb`  | One step. `href` makes it a link; without one it is current |

**The sheet has no breadcrumb in it**, so the arrangement is an invention — but every visible part is
borrowed: the sheet's own `.ds-link-caps` for the steps, its softest line tone for the punctuation,
and its muted-to-full-strength hierarchy for the trail above you.

### React Aria renders the list and not the landmark

`Breadcrumbs` is an `<ol>` — **no `<nav>` around it and no role on the list.** The first version of this
component was therefore a list of links sitting in no landmark at all, so a screen reader's landmark
list offered no way to reach it. A breadcrumb _is_ navigation; the wrapper is this component's job, so
`Breadcrumbs` draws the `<nav aria-label>` itself and the `label` prop goes there rather than through
to React Aria.

### The slash is a pseudo-element, and that is right here

It belongs to the item, not to the list, and `last:after:content-none` is what stops a trail ending in
a stray `/`. A pseudo-element is correct for it — a slash carries no text, cannot be pressed and needs
no accessible name — which is exactly why the caret in `Nav` could **not** be one.

### The steps are `shrink-0`

Without it a flex item happily narrows mid-word, so three steps sat on one line in a 176px container
with every word squeezed and `flex-wrap` never had anything to wrap. `Wraps` found it.

### A link that really navigates kills the test runner

Worth knowing before writing an interaction story about anchors. `userEvent.click` on a step with a
real `href` **navigates the story's own frame away**, and the symptom is `[vitest] Browser connection
was closed while running tests` with three of six stories passing and no failing story named at all —
because the runner never got to name one. The `Keyboard` story now asserts that every step is a
reachable anchor at `tabIndex 0` and **does not press it**. Following a link is the browser's job.

### The type belongs to the link

A step is a caps link, and the **link owns its type** — `.ds-link-caps` at 14px and `-0.01em`, with
`--lg` the only larger size the sheet has. A font size on the item would lose the cascade to the
link's anyway, and pretending otherwise made the assertion wrong twice before it was deleted.
